finding_key: packages/backend/scripts/migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts::bulk yorkie data-migration scripts will mass-bump every document's new `updatedat` once the webhook is registered, destroying list ordering fleet-wide
evidence: The mechanism is coherent and matches the supplied code: both maintenance scripts mutate the Yorkie root (`migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts` `doc.update(... migrateConditionalFormatRanges ...)` + `client.sync`, and `migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts` `replaceYorkieRoot` + `client.sync`), and the new ingestion path (`yorkie-event.controller.ts` `touchUpdatedAt(parsed.id, min(issuedAt, now))`) has no notion of "this was a migration, not a user edit", while `document.controller.ts:116,148` now sorts by that column — so a migration run would stamp migrated docs with the migration time and wipe edit-recency ordering. Two things temper the claim's framing: both scripts only `doc.update`/`sync` when `changed` is true, so it is *not* "every document in the DB" — only rows the legacy migration actually rewrites; and because both scripts iterate `createdAt asc`, the resulting order collapses to roughly `createdAt desc`, i.e. the pre-PR default, and self-heals on each document's next real edit. I could not verify Yorkie's event semantics (whether an admin-SDK root write emits `DocumentRootChanged`) from source here, and the webhook is not registered yet per the todo's open ops item, so the failure requires two conditions to line up — hence medium confidence and minor severity rather than a blocking defect.
